text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: autocritical - metrics-pipeline-prod - high scrape error rate (429) and log-ingest backlog. Page fired to eng-sre.
oncall-sre: acked. I'm on it, joining now.
alex: looking at prometheus scrape job metrics, we're seeing a sudden spike of 429s from the exporter fleet around the same time as a customer traffic burst.
maya: confirmed. Prom scrape_errors_total has +1200 in the last 5m, error reason=429. exporter HTTP responses show "rate limit" headers.
samir: kafka-consumer groups for log-ingest are showing consumer_lag > 50k for a few partitions, likely caused by downstream processing spikes.
oncall-sre: quick triage - is this exporter-side throttling (external upstream) or our scrape rate/concurrency?
alex: headers suggest upstream (exporter reports 429, x-rate-limit-* present). But also our scrape concurrency has been at max (scrape_configs.relabel_configs unchanged). worth reducing scrape parallelism for low-priority jobs.
maya: initiating mitigation: temporarily pausing non-critical scrape targets (k8s:kube-state|node-exporter lowcard) for prod to free requests. Posting commands:
```
# annotate then pause
kubectl -n monitoring annotate prometheus/prom-main redwood.sre/paused-targets="lowcard"
kubectl -n monitoring patch prometheus/prom-main --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/scrapeInterval","value":"30s"}]'  # temp
```
tess: deployed a consumer-scale bump for log-ingest: bumped replicas from 4 -> 8 for consumers/ingest-proc-prod. Watching lag.
oncall-sre: good. alex, can you change scrape timeout to 15s for heavy exporters to avoid building more pending connections?
alex: done. Patch applied to prometheus config, reloading: `kubectl rollout restart statefulset/prom-main -n monitoring`.
samir: consumer lag dropping slowly, backpressure clearing on downstream processors. some customer dashboards will show small gaps for ~10-20m.
oncall-sre: customer-impact check: any paid customers reporting missing metrics or alerts firing?
maya: no external PD pages reported yet, but internal dashboards show missing node_cpu* metrics for some clusters. I sent an ops-notify to #customer-ops with ETA ~20m.
oncall-sre: pinging exporter's owners... alex where are the exporter svc pods?
alex: exporter/frontend-metrics is in infra namespace. logs show 429s and bursts of requests from our side. I opened a connection with them: `kubectl logs -n infra deploy/exporter-frontend -c main | tail -n 200` showed rate limiter warnings.
```
W 2026-03-14T12:34:12Z rate_limiter.go:89 throttled request from 10.0.12.45
```

maya: exporter owners responded - they recently rolled out a strict rate-limit to protect a downstream dependency. They're increasing per-ip quota but need a safe ramp window.
oncall-sre: plan: 1) keep low-priority scrapes paused and longer interval; 2) keep increased consumer replicas until backlog clears; 3) coordinate with exporter team to raise quota; 4) run canary re-enable of one target to confirm stability; 5) track customer impact and notify.

samir: I'm keeping an eye on kafka lag and will scale further if needed. If lag stops decreasing in 10m we escalate to infra-scaling.

oncall-sre: handoff note for next on-call in 30m: leave paused-scrapes annotation in place, consumer replicas at 8, and coordinate with exporter team on quota change. I'll update incident log.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: prom-main reload succeeded (revision 12 -> 13).

maya: backlog is down 40% in 8m. exporter's quota bump applied by infra team (confirmed). re-enabling one low-priority target now as canary.
alex: canary scrape returned 200 for 5 consecutive attempts. re-enable in waves.
oncall-sre: marking page as mitigated for now. leaving postmortem TODO: explain why autodetection didn't throttle/route scrapes, consider implementing target-priority-based partial backoff.
tess: noted for action item: add a runbook step to auto-pause low-priority scrapes when exporter 429 threshold exceeded.
samir: final check: consumer lag ~3k and trending to zero.
oncall-sre: thanks all. I'll post incident summary and schedule follow-up with exporter owners and monitoring infra next week. closing thread once backlog cleared and dashboards stable. :thumbsup:
